heuristics: r-adding walk with r=2^24 behaves as a random mapping on negation classes (Teske 2001); the claim needs a walk-quality factor of at least 0.9076, against a finite-r Brent-Pollard correction of 1+2^-25 at r=2^24 and measured deviations of a few percent at r=20

cycles of up to 64 classes are detected by a fixed 64-step checkpoint of the full 256-bit canonical u and escaped from the cycle's smallest-u member through a separate escape table, so merged walks stay merged; re-entry into a cycle just escaped is bounded by its basin at 2^-135.4 per cycle and the whole cycle loss, including cycles longer than 64 classes, at 2^-9.19 of all steps (budget 2^-9)
distinguished-point positions (bits 0..95 of u) are independent of the table index (bits 232..255) and of the escape index (bits 224..231); the three bit fields are disjoint
limitations: Analytic cost bound; no production-size execution.

Field multiplication and modular add/sub are counted from an explicit AArch64 instruction listing (p256_mul_count.md) checked by executing it under the AArch64 flag rules (check_mul_mont.py); the other per-step items are itemised upper bounds (proof.md section 4) and no P-256 kernel was measured; compiler spills are not priced.

The cycle bounds are model bounds (a counting argument for short cycles, a random-mapping basin expectation for re-entry, a zero-sum closure estimate for cycles longer than 64 classes); the score is insensitive to them up to a cycle budget of 2^-8.72.
The toy experiment in experiment.py supports the walk and cycle mechanism only at toy scale.
Not a novel attack; textbook generic rho with the negation map.
